questions.q: According to this lesson, why should the safety decisions (read-only role, validation) be presented as a core part of the walkthrough rather than an aside mentioned if there's time?
options: They are not actually important to this project
They're the part most portfolio projects skip and most interviewers specifically probe on
Interviewers never ask about security
They take too long to explain and should be skipped
questions.explain: An interviewer who has seen many basic chatbot demos is likely to ask pointed questions about exactly this project's safety decisions -- presenting them clearly shows you understand why they matter, not just that you added them.

questions.q: What is the five-part structure this lesson recommends for presenting Project 2?
options: Code, tests, deployment, pricing, roadmap
The problem, the architecture, the safety decisions, the demo, and known limitations
Introduction, body, conclusion, references, appendix
Database, API, frontend, backend, infrastructure
questions.explain: This order leads with the real question being solved, traces the architecture, surfaces the safety reasoning, demonstrates it live, and closes with an honest account of what's not yet handled.

questions.q: Why does this lesson recommend writing a specific 'known limitations' section instead of only showing a polished happy-path demo?
options: It is required by the Messages API
A specific, honest limitations list is more credible and shows you understand the system's actual boundaries
Limitations sections are only needed for failing projects
It replaces the need for a working demo entirely
questions.explain: Naming real gaps -- like no caching layer or untested prompt-injection resistance -- demonstrates genuine understanding of the system, which is more impressive than implying it's airtight.

questions.q: What distinct risk does this lesson name that the Lesson 10 query validation does NOT defend against?
options: SQL injection through string concatenation
A user attempting to manipulate Claude's reasoning through the wording of their natural-language question itself
The database running out of disk space
The exchange-rate API being deprecated
questions.explain: Query validation defends the generated SQL text, but a cleverly worded question could still attempt to manipulate the model's reasoning -- a different, not-yet-tested risk this lesson flags as an honest limitation.

questions.q: Which lesson comes immediately after this one, per the course outline?
options: Lesson 13, Project 3 Kickoff
Lesson 9, Connecting to a Database Safely
Lesson 1, Program Overview & Portfolio Strategy
Lesson 23, Salary Negotiation & Next Steps
